sections.html:
Tift County is the small, dense county around Tifton in south central Georgia. Tifton is the seat and largest city, Omega and Ty Ty are the other cities, and Phillipsburg and Unionville are census-designated places. Chula and Brookfield are unincorporated. Interstate 75 runs through the county, and a single school system, the Tift County School District, runs the public schools countywide.

Tift packs in 158.5 people per square mile, and owners occupy 61.0% of housing units for 2020-2024. Headcount is up 2.2% since April 2020. With 41.6% of occupied homes rented, a Tifton house with a tenant already in it can attract a landlord-minded buyer. Mention the lease at the start and let the buyer judge.

sections.h2: Which offices bill and which values
sections.html:
The commissioner collects the money and then sends it on to the state, the county, the city and the school board. Values come from the assessors. Two separate offices, two separate phone lines.

The tax commissioner takes mail at P.O. Box 930, Tifton, GA 31793, answers at (229) 386-7820, and stays open on weekdays from half past eight until five. The tax assessors take mail at P.O. Box 134, Tifton, GA 31793, and answer at (229) 386-7840 from eight to five, Monday through Friday.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, online payments, delinquent accounts, tax sales
  • Tax assessors: real and personal property values, mobile home decal reviews, exemptions
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and executions

The commissioner's office also collects city taxes, so one office can answer for a Tifton address and an unincorporated one.

The regular bill is due November 15 and the mobile home bill April 1.

Installments are welcome online for property tax. No minimum opens a payment plan, since the office names an amount once arrangements are made so the balance clears on schedule. Mobile home owners can pay in pieces too, with the decal withheld until nothing is left owing.

  • Property tax: November 15
  • Mobile home tax: April 1
  • Partial payments: accepted online for property tax
  • Decal: issued only after a mobile home balance is paid in full

Clearing a delinquent bill does not hand over the property. That settles any rumor to the contrary.

The bill starts with the assessor's market value as of January 1, then takes 40% of it as the assessed value. Subtract any homestead exemption from that assessed value, including the state's standard $2,000 exemption, and multiply the remainder by the millage rate.

One mill is a dollar of tax per thousand dollars of assessed value. Tift County officials set their own part of the rate, the school board sets its part, and the state adds a small levy of its own. Cities that levy a tax add a further rate on top, which is why two houses with the same value can receive different bills.

  • Step one: market value on January 1
  • Step two: 40% of that value, less exemptions
  • Step three: multiply by the combined millage rate

The county website links to an online parcel search, so you can look up your own value, owner of record and acreage before talking to either office. Check the acreage and the building description for errors, because a wrong square footage carries straight into the bill.

It usually means an appraiser is checking on a change. Homes that traded hands during the previous 12 months get a field review, and O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 sets the notice rule.

Further triggers: a permit for a remodel, pool or outbuilding, a reported fire or storm loss, a parcel split or merger, and an application for a covenant or exemption. Field work clusters between December and May. Staff arrive in a marked county vehicle with identification, and an owner who prefers a set time can book one at (229) 386-7840.

If you just finished permitted work, expect the next notice to show a higher value. Hold on to the permit and photos of the house before the work, which help if you contest the new figure.

The levying office notifies the delinquent taxpayer in writing, and 30 days later an execution, called a fi. fa., can follow on the General Execution Docket kept by the superior court clerk. The lien on property attaches every January 1, even before any execution exists.

That officer acts as ex-officio sheriff and may advertise and auction the parcel. These are buyer-beware sales, opening at the taxes, penalties and costs owed. The winner gets a sheriff's tax deed, which is not a fee simple deed, and state law bars possession for 12 months while redemption rights remain.

A seller gains nothing from reaching that stage. Ring (229) 386-7820 and get a payoff figure in hand before you list or take an offer. A house that is behind on tax and in rough shape can also go to a cash buyer who buys as-is and accounts for the tax. That route skips repairs, showings and the wait on a buyer's loan, and the payoff comes out of the proceeds at closing.

Submit the appeal in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. Forty-five days run from the day the notice was mailed. The permitted grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

Your first filing has to pick a forum: the equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration. State staff cannot override local boards on one parcel. Assessment is set at 40% of fair market value, so compare the market value on the notice with recent sales of similar homes near you. Attach what you find to the appeal.

faqs.q: Where do I reach the Tift County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: Call (229) 386-7820 or write to P.O. Box 930, Tifton, GA 31793. Weekday hours begin at 8:30 in the morning and end at 5 in the afternoon.

faqs.q: Are installments allowed for Tift County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, the county takes partial payments online. No fixed amount starts the plan, and the office sets one after you make arrangements. Mobile home owners can split payments as well but get the decal only once they have paid everything.

faqs.q: Does clearing a delinquent bill give me the property in Tift County?
faqs.a: No. Paying delinquent tax does not transfer ownership. Auction buyers get a sheriff's tax deed and, under state law, wait 12 months after the sale before taking possession.

faqs.q: Who collects city tax inside Tifton?
faqs.a: The Tift County tax commissioner does. The office collects city taxes and distributes funds to the state, the county and the school board as well.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for contesting a Tift County value?
faqs.a: The cutoff is 45 days after the assessment notice was mailed. Send your appeal to the Tift County assessors, phone (229) 386-7840 with questions, and pick your path on the form.
